newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire's first woman governor takes office.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire's first woman governor takes office.

text.p: Jeanne Shaheen Thursday became New Hampshire's first woman governor and the first Democratic governor this northeastern bastion of the Republican Party has seen in 16 years.

A former state senator who ran the presidential primary campaigns of Jimmy Carter and Gary Hart, Shaheen took office promising to improve public education, lower electric rates, protect health care, create jobs and build up the state's economy.

Shaheen, 49, reiterated her pledge to veto any new income or sales tax that might come to her desk, in line with past Republican governors who have taken the famous New Hampshire pledge against broad-based taxes.
"I said it during my campaign and I will say it again now," Shaheen said. "I will not propose or support such a tax, and if this legislature passes one I will veto it."
Shaheen said while the tradition of The Pledge will continue, other "traditions" such as "high electric rates" and declining public education will end under her administration.

New Hampshire has among the highest electric rates in the United States because of the state's top utility's investment in the Seabrook nuclear power plant. Because of massive cost overruns and alledged mismanagement at Seabrook, the utility was allowed rate increases of 5.5 percent a year for seven years beginning in 1990.
As a legislator, Shaheen led the fight to deregulate the state's electric utilities.
As governor, introducing competition will be a top priority, she said.

"For too long we have been paying the highest electric rates in the nation. They constitute a hidden tax, taking money away from families already struggling to make ends meet. They are increasing the costs of running our businesses, our towns and our state," Shaheen said.
Shaheen also pledged to expand kindergarten programmes throughout the state, but did not offer specifics about how New Hampshire would pay for expanded schooling.
Shaheen succeeds Republican Gov. Stephen Merrill, an outspoken conservative and former chairman of presidential candidate Bob Dole's campaign.
Merrill is seeking to be the next chairman of the Republican National Committee.
